TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  MINUTES
  AUGUST 14, 2019

  1.  CHAIR SCHMITZ called the meeting to order at 6:12 p.m.

  2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Schmitz, Pope, Combs, Martin, Vanden Bos

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Scott, Boothe, Lum, Munday

  ALSO PRESENT: Deputy Bouse

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development and Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES, MEETING OF MAY 8, 2019

  COMMITTEE MEMBER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  MARTIN to,

  APPROVE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MAY 8, 2019

  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  None

  5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A.  MOCCASIN LANE – CONSIDERATION OF ADDITIONAL TRAFFIC CONTROLS

  Director Wahba stated that a request was submitted by Christine Costantini regarding concerns
  for pedestrians crossing Moccasin Lane and the on-street parking during school drop-off and
  pick-up hours.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided an overview of the work done by LA County on
  Moccasin Lane with red curbs and signage; the installation of a new sign at 15 Moccasin is
  pending.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there is a lot of on-street parking during school
  hours and observed most vehicles travel at 25-30 mph and a few a bit faster. She observed that
  it is difficult to see pedestrians at the crosswalk especially when vehicles are parked on the
  street. The options that were presented were:

  •  Installation of a bulb-out.
  •  Flexible school crossing sign, which is a narrow sign that says, “Yield to Pedestrians”.
  •  Install ADA ramps, which could be in conjunction with the bulb-out.
  •  Installation of edgelines.
  •  Radar speed trailer.
  •  Decoy enforcement vehicle.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS inquired if consideration has been given to relocating
  the crosswalk. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki explained factors which make moving the
  crosswalk difficult, but stated that this could be a consideration.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS asked about sensors that would cause the crosswalk to light
  up when pedestrians are crossing. Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there are in-

   roadway warning lights at Palos Verdes Drive North and Moccasin and this could be a
  consideration, but it must meet guideline requirements.

  Angela Conterno, Moccasin Lane resident, stated that her home is located where vehicles
  turnaround and expressed her concern with the speed that vehicles travel on their street and
  the amount of vehicles parked waiting for children. Ms. Conterno suggested that a flashing sign
  would be helpful to get people to carefully cross the street. A decoy car would also be helpful.

  Christine Costantini, Moccasin Lane resident, expressed her concern with vehicles parking on
  both sides of the crosswalk which creates a blind spot for oncoming traffic and pedestrians
  cannot be seen. Ms. Costantini suggested that people begin getting ticketed when parked
  illegally. She expressed her concerns with the safety for pedestrians. She stated that in addition
  to school, traffic is impacted by the church and access to the landfill which is a popular dog
  walking spot. Ms. Costantini agreed with the suggestion of a decoy car.

  Linus Yeh, Moccasin Lane resident, stated that traffic is a concern and stated that vehicles are
  parked in red zones; this causes near accidents with oncoming traffic since vehicles must drive
  on the wrong side of the street.

  Christopher Yeh, Moccasin Lane resident, stated that more parking could be a solution and
  agreed that there needs to be enforcement.

  Mr. Yeh agreed with enforcement by way of ticketing illegally parked vehicles.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that any changes to the street should be sent for review by the
  neighborhood so that they have an opportunity to comment. Moccasin Lane does not have a
  formal HOA.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ summarized that there is consensus on the following:

  •  Signage changed to the new neon color.
  •  Request of the decoy car.
  •  Awareness/enforcement of the red curb.

  Deputy Bouse expressed her concern with enforcing the red curb, which will further impact
  traffic on Palos Verdes Drive North.

  Ms. Costantini added that enforcement specific to the vehicles parked in the crosswalk is
  necessary.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS suggested that the school send out notices specific to
  the concern related to the vehicles parked in the crosswalk.

  Ms. Costantini stated that she will ask the principal of Rancho Vista to send a notice
  regarding illegally parking on the red curb at either side of the crosswalk and that violators
  will be ticketed.

  Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that she would like to provide the neighborhood with
  options from the committee. Ms. Conterno has agreed to be the contact for the neighborhood
  as she is active in the neighborhood watch and has contact information for all residents on
  Moccasin Lane.

  A discussion ensued with concerns regarding installing of a bulb out and the other options
  presented. Further discussion ensued regarding cars parked on the red curb on both sides of
  the street.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS suggested that only one side of the street be painted
  red.

  A discussion ensued on this option.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that she is in agreement that the e-mail from the school should be sent;
  ticketing vehicles parked at the crosswalk; and, to inquire with the neighborhood on the options
  discussed.

   COMMITTEE MEMBER COMBS stated that the red curb is intended for emergency personnel
  and suggested that vehicles parked in the red curb should also be enforced and/or reevaluate
  is both sides of the street need to be a red curb.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ stated that this item will be continued to the next Traffic and Safety Committee
  meeting.

  6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS (VERBAL REPORTS)

  A.  VERBAL UPDATE ON TRAFFIC AND SAFETY ITEMS

  Director Wahba stated that Palos Verdes Drive North between Dapplegray Lane and
  Rolling Hills Road is being repaved and the work will be completed by August 16th.

  Director Wahba stated that the storm drain repair project at Palos Verdes Drive East and
  Club View Lane started this week and the work will be completed by August 16th.

  Director Wahba stated that there are streets in Rolling Hills Estates, which include Whitley
  Collins Drive, Quailwood Drive, Stonecrest Road, and Scotwood Drive, will be repaved as
  a part of a Rancho Palos Verdes repaving project.

  7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS stated that the timing of the signal at Palos Verdes
  Drive North needs to be adjusted for southbound left turn traffic.

  8.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ adjourned the meeting at 7:12 p.m. The next Traffic and Safety Committee
  meeting will be held on Wednesday, November 13, 2019 at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council
  Chamber located at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
  Estates, California.
